Canada is an immigrant nation. Our grandfathers came through Pier 21 with nothing but determination and a name on a manifest. They built the railroads, harvested the prairies, manned the convoys. The system worked — because it was managed . There were targets tied to capacity. Housing was affordable. Hospitals had beds. Schools had desks.

What's happening now isn't immigration — it's policy malpractice . When the intake exceeds every support system's capacity, when processing backlogs leave families in limbo for years, when the Temporary Foreign Worker program suppresses wages across entire sectors — the failure isn't at the border. It's in Ottawa.
"They came through the front door, signed the book, and built this country. Now the door has no hinges, the book has no pages, and nobody's building anything but condos."
